assumptions: The family installer participates only through a voluntary arm's-length pilot and supplies no exclusive customer, technician, or confidential-data rights.
Installers may lawfully subcontract the scoped work and suitable manufacturer-specific authorizations can be checked before dispatch.
Professional liability coverage and technician contracts are obtainable within the stated initial capital envelope.
The proposed reservation and dispatch prices exclude material parts and can be changed after a paid pilot without breaking the concept.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid multi-installer pilot should show callback arrival rates by postcode and device, reservation conversion and renewal, dispatch acceptance, travel time, technician fill rate, first-visit resolution, repeat work, credits, fully loaded contribution margin, and whether installers permit the operator to coordinate service without harming warranties or customer trust.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Pooling intermittent installer callback demand against pre-reserved technician capacity is a coherent response to the mismatch between peak service load and the cost of permanent staff. URE reports 1,636,673 Polish renewable microinstallations at year-end 2025, 99.9% photovoltaic, which supports a large installed-service surface, but it does not establish callback frequency or economically poolable demand.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Urgent faults, warranty callbacks, travel, and customer dissatisfaction create credible pain for installers, and service-response obligations can be commercially important. However, there is no buyer interview, paid pilot, callback ledger, or evidence that small installers will pay a fixed monthly reservation rather than use ad hoc subcontractors; third-party work can also threaten warranty status and the installer's customer relationship.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Advance reservation billing plus a per-dispatch spread offers favorable cash conversion and could pool capacity efficiently. The proposed prices, CAC recovery, 20-35% dispatch contribution, utilization, travel radius, repeat-visit rate, and credit burden are all unvalidated, while correlated seasonal demand can make the business lose money both when reserved hours sit idle and when peak demand exceeds reserved supply. The 600-installer wealth path would require a materially larger and more operationally complex network than the initial model demonstrates.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: A defined western/central Poland service radius and small-to-midsize installers form a sensible regional beachhead, supported by a large installed PV base. Yet the candidate gives no count of reachable payer firms, service incidents, or spend, and combining photovoltaic, battery, and heat-pump work at launch makes the technical beachhead less focused than the geography suggests.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Local dispatch density and reliable SLA performance could earn a strong regional reputation, but current control is only nonexclusive, short-duration access to replaceable technicians. Manufacturer partner networks, wholesaler service functions, direct subcontractors, and national multibrand service networks already occupy adjacent positions, so a dominant position would require demonstrated density or privileged demand aggregation not yet present.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful single-zone model could expand to neighboring regions, batteries, heat pumps, preventive inspections, remote triage, monitoring, warranty administration, and parts coordination. Those adjacencies share installer relationships and incident data, although every geographic or equipment expansion adds field-supply, training, authorization, and quality-control work.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Route density, observed failure codes, technician performance histories, and an SLA reputation could compound with scale. The initial asset is nevertheless six-month nonexclusive capacity from technicians found through public channels; installers, manufacturers, wholesalers, or a better-funded dispatcher can reproduce the contracting model, and the proposed data advantage is useful only after substantial verified volume.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Neutral multibrand coverage with a guaranteed local response window could be materially more convenient than locating a technician incident by incident. The benefit has not been benchmarked against an installer's own subcontractors, and public competitors already advertise nationwide coverage, multibrand work, tracking, warranties, or response in as little as 48 hours, so the claimed advantage is not yet sufficient to predict behavior change.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Poland's very large and aging prosumer PV base is shifting economic attention from installation toward lifecycle service, while batteries and heat pumps broaden the aftercare surface. Recent evidence also points to slower new-install growth and installer price pressure, which can increase appetite for variable capacity, though it can equally create excess technician supply and price competition.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: A voluntary pilot with the family installer, public UDT prospecting data, technician referrals, and focused regional outbound make the first conversations realistically accessible without a personal media brand. Repeatable acquisition remains uncertain because service outsourcing is trust-heavy, the public register proves certification rather than availability or buying intent, and wholesaler referrals are proposed but not committed.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's quantitative skills and family-sector access help with triage design and a bounded pilot, and 75,000 PLN can plausibly fund validation. Safe multibrand field work, insurance, manufacturer authorization, technician vetting, scheduling, rework, and response coverage are operationally demanding; a part-time founder cannot personally cover the service window, while an early dispatcher adds fixed cost before density is proven.

highest_value_structural_change: Start with one equipment class and one compact service zone, obtain prepaid SLA commitments and minimum dispatch volumes from several unrelated installers before reserving technician blocks, and maintain a manufacturer-authorization matrix so capacity purchases are backed by demand and warranty-compatible scope.
main_structural_strength: The model turns volatile service overflow into prepaid recurring revenue while pooling replaceable technician capacity across multiple installers inside a bounded geography.
primary_score_limiter: No evidence yet establishes incident density, reservation willingness to pay, or the utilization and travel profile needed for the promised SLA to produce attractive contribution margin rather than field-service losses.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The closest contrary evidence is that existing providers already advertise nationwide or manufacturer-backed service: Serwis112 claims a verified nationwide network and response in as little as 48 hours (https://serwis112.pl/), while Fronius maintains trained service partners and some Plus partners accept systems they did not install (https://www.fronius.com/pl-pl/poland/energia-sloneczna/firmy/kontakt/znajdz-instalatora). This weakens novelty and shows installers may have channel alternatives, although neither source proves the proposed B2B reservation model lacks demand.
